components.css: .ds-card-post { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; width: 75%; margin: 0 auto; padding: 20px; background: #ffffff; color: #18181b; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(2,6,23,0.8), 0 2px 4px -2px rgba(2,6,23,0.8); transition: all 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); text-decoration: none; } .ds-card-post:hover { box-shadow: 0 20px 25px -5px rgba(2,6,23,0.7), 0 8px 10px -6px rgba(2,6,23,0.7); cursor: pointer; } .ds-card-post-header { display: flex; align-items: center; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-card-post-title { font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; margin: 0; } .ds-card-post:hover .ds-card-post-title { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 2px; } .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 4px; border-radius: 6px; color: #ffffff; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.875rem; margin-left: auto; } .ds-badge-open { background: #9333ea; } .ds-badge-closed { background: #10b981; } .ds-card-post-content { display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; } .ds-card-post-footer { margin-top: auto; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; } .ds-metric { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; margin-right: 16px; } .ds-metric-ratio { color: #f59e0b; } .ds-metric-views { color: #3b82f6; } .ds-metric-likes { color: #f43f5e; } .ds-tag { font-size: 0.875rem; margin-right: 16px; } .ds-date { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #3f3f46; }

narrative.overview:
ForUm's design is built around the feeling of a well-worn table where people gather to share ideas. The interface is clean and purposeful — spacious, high-contrast, and deliberately quiet so the conversation itself fills the room. Cards sit on a slate surface like paper scattered across a tabletop, gently lifted to suggest they can be picked up and engaged with. Every element either serves reading, writing, or navigating the discussion; chrome exists only to make those actions feel tactile and dependable.

The palette stays neutral (slate backgrounds, white cards, zinc text) so that the status badges, interactive buttons, and user-generated markdown content become the color moments. This is not a brand that needs to shout — it's a table that welcomes anyone to sit down and write.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral canvas with deliberate color accents for functional feedback
Cards always gently lifted; hover deepens the elevation
Tactile, bold interactive states — buttons feel clickable, fields feel editable
High contrast between surface zones (slate feed / white cards)
Spacious internal rhythms (16–20px padding on containers)
Underlined navigation links with a scale-in animation on hover

rules.name: The One-Color-Rule
rules.body: A single accent color is used per functional zone. Status badges get their own color (green/purple); action buttons get blue/orange; engagement metrics get amber/rose. They never blend into a single palette gradient — each color carries distinct meaning.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Every text element on screen uses the same font family stack. Hierarchy comes from weight, size, and spacing — never from a font swap.

rules.name: The Lifted-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards always carry a shadow. The baseline elevation is not zero — content surfaces that can be interacted with are always visually lifted from the background.

dos: Do use shadow-md as the minimum card elevation. Cards must feel lifted from the slate surface.
Do reserve color for functional meaning. Green = resolved, Purple = open, Blue = action, Orange = register, Red = danger.
Do use the underline-scale animation for navigation links — it's the system's signature micro-interaction.
Do keep content cards white on the slate-800 feed background for maximum figure-ground clarity.
Do use brightness-90 for button hover states — it's the consistent, predictable feedback pattern.
donts: Don't add shadows to buttons. Button state is communicated through background color and brightness, not elevation.
Don't use rounded corners larger than 8px — the system is defined by subtle (rounded-md) curvature.
Don't mix input styles. All text inputs use the underline (border-b-2) pattern — no bordered boxes.
Don't introduce a secondary font family — Inter serves all roles via weight and size contrast.
Don't place accent colors on backgrounds — the slate feed + white card pattern is the invariant surface relationship.
